message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide that shows **how** most modern DNS‑management APIs let you pull *only* the `id` field and whatever “context” metadata you’re interested in—without pulling the full record payload.  
(The exact URL path, header names, and query‑string keys will vary slightly between vendors – see each vendor’s docs for the precise values.)

---

### 1️⃣ Build the request

| Piece | What it means |
|-------|---------------|
| **Endpoint** | `/v1/domains/{domain}/records/caa` (or similar) |
| **HTTP method** | `GET` |
| **Auth header** | `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>` |
| **Query params** | `fields=` or `select=` – comma‑separated list of columns you want |

#### Example (generic)

```bash
curl -X GET \
     -H "Accept: application/json" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer secret567" \
     "https://api.dnsprovider.example/v1/domains/sample2.com/records/caa?fields=id,context"
```

> **Tip:** If the provider uses GraphQL instead of REST, you’d send something like:
>
> ```graphql
> {
>   caaRecords(domain:"sample2.com") { id context }
> }
> ```

---

### 2️⃣ Typical JSON shape returned

```json
{
  "data": [
    {"id":"caas_001","context":{"created_at":"2025-01-12T08:34Z"}},
    {"id":"caas_002","context":{"updated_by":"admin"}}
  ],
  "meta": {...}
}
```

Only the requested fields (`id`, `context`) appear inside each object.

---

### 3️⃣ Common pitfalls & fixes  

| Problem | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| You still receive extra fields | Double‑check the parameter name (`fields`, `select`, `_fields`). Some APIs require a prefix like `include=...`. |
| Context isn’t populated | Make sure the context attribute is part of the schema. It might live under another nested key (`metadata.context`). Adjust the selector accordingly. |
| Pagination hides data | Add `page_size=<n>&page_token=<token>` until all pages return. Most services also allow `limit=0` to fetch everything at once. |

---

### 4️⃣ Vendor‑specific notes

| Provider | How to specify minimal fields |
|----------|------------------------------|
| Cloudflare | `?match=all&per_page=100&page=1&content_type=caa` + parse out `id` manually (no built‑in projection). |
| AWS Route 53 | No native field projection; retrieve whole recordset then slice client‑side. |
| DigitalOcean | Supports `?filter[record_id]=true` – returns only ID plus basic meta. |
| Google Domains | Uses `view=summary` flag to limit detail. |
| Namecheap | Requires custom script after fetching full list because they don’t expose projections. |

If you can share which platform you’re working against, I can tailor the snippet even more precisely!

--- 

Let me know if you hit any snags while wiring this up—or if you need help crafting the exact query string for a particular DNS service!
